title: Log quarantine list
prompt: The platform team wants every line of the log file accounted for, so broken lines can be traced back to the shipper. Write `solve(application_logs_raw)` so it returns `log_id`, `service` and `bad_record` for every non-blank line: `bad_record` is the raw line when it couldn't be parsed, and NULL otherwise.
rules: One row per non-blank line, good or bad. Keep repeated lines.
For a line that isn't valid JSON, `log_id` and `service` are NULL and `bad_record` is the line exactly as it arrived.
A file with no bad lines still has a `bad_record` column, all NULL.
Return only `log_id`, `service` and `bad_record` (all text), in that order.
hints: Read with a schema that ends in a text column for the raw line.
The default mode keeps bad lines; `columnNameOfCorruptRecord` names the column that gets their text.
Without a schema, `_corrupt_record` only exists when some line is bad. A schema makes the column always there.
starter:
def solve(application_logs_raw):
    path = "/tmp/logs/app"
    application_logs_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    # Read the file at `path` and return log_id, service and bad_record for every line.
    return application_logs_raw
